div.p: B-good turns preferential procurement into a live operating view. It tracks spend, supplier compliance, evidence readiness, and score movement in one place so leaders can act sooner.

div.class: card p-4 shadow-sm border-0 bg-white mb-3 doc-section-card
div.data-keywords: module overview handbook guide platform story b-good purpose executive summary
div.p: This module is the commercial control layer for preferential procurement inside B-good. It unifies score visibility, supplier evidence, spend exposure, and verification preparation into a single operational workspace so procurement and finance teams can move from reactive reporting to active management.

The design assumption behind the module is simple: procurement value only matters when it is both commercially useful and defensible during review. Every screen in the app is meant to help the business understand where value is protected, where it is exposed, and what actions will improve the score the fastest.

The module functions independently of legacy ledger constraints, creating an isolated staging area where simulation rules can be executed safely before values are committed to production compliance targets.

div.class: card p-4 shadow-sm border-0 bg-white mb-3 doc-section-card
div.data-keywords: scorecard mechanics levels points thresholds live score target threshold recognition penalty legislative requirements
div.p: The scorecard is the executive summary of preferential procurement performance. It consolidates supplier compliance, recognised spend, evidence quality, and risk exposure into one live view so a leadership team can see whether the business is moving toward stronger recognition or drifting into audit vulnerability.

The system monitors cumulative target targets across sub-minimum requirements. Failing to meet a sub-minimum automatically triggers a recognition penalty, which downgrades the overall tier output regardless of point total. That means the headline level is not just a vanity figure; it is a compact representation of how effectively the organisation has converted spend into compliant value.

span.class: text-uppercase small font-weight-bold text-muted d-block mb-1

ul.li: Live score: The real-time performance indicator that moves as new spend batches are imported or evidence states change.
Level 1-8: The current B-BBEE position, calculated from recognition outcomes and threshold alignment.
Next level: The precise points gap required to elevate the organisation into the next tier.

div.p: Operationally, this gives procurement committees a way to predict score movement before the year closes. It also creates a consistent language for finance, compliance, and buyers to discuss risk without needing to interpret spreadsheets manually.

Dynamic target targets are assessed per legislative sub-weight. If a company fails a core threshold element, the system automatically triggers an optimization prompt within the user dashboard to guide mitigation paths.

div.class: card p-4 shadow-sm border-0 bg-white mb-3 doc-section-card
div.data-keywords: supplier compliance profiles certificates affidavits verification disputed expired missing recognition credentials supplier node
div.p: Supplier compliance is the proof layer beneath the scorecard. Every supplier entity acts as an asset node. When a verification agency challenges a vendor's credentials, changing the status flag to 'Disputed' instantly triggers a cascading recalculation across all historical spend streams referencing that node.

In practical terms, supplier records are not passive contact cards. They are the system’s trust anchors. Their recognition percentage, B-BBEE level, and current evidence state determine whether spend can be counted, whether it must be isolated for manual review, and whether it will reinforce or weaken the organisation’s score at reporting time.

Because supplier profiles serve as the foundation for enterprise spend attribution, changing any individual vendor's B-BBEE rating forces an automated background analysis across all matching invoice rows inside the active fiscal year.

div.span: When supplier evidence is current, recognised spend flows cleanly into the scorecard with less reconciliation overhead.

div.class: card p-4 shadow-sm border-0 bg-white mb-3 doc-section-card
div.data-keywords: spend batches ingestion ledger normalized vat quarantine unmapped transactions accounting logs recognised spend
div.p: Spend management bridges the gap between raw accounting ledgers and the compliance score. Raw accounting logs are normalized during state ingestion. The ledger processor matches VAT registration strings against active database records, routing unmapped items into a quarantine ledger for manual assignment.

The process is intentionally strict because recognition quality depends on the quality of the underlying match. If a transaction cannot be tied to an active supplier record or the evidence state is weak, the engine treats that value as exposed rather than automatically optimistic. That prevents inflated recognition claims and makes the control environment auditable.

p.em: Note: Unmapped transactions represent critical data leakage and should be assigned to an active supplier entity immediately to prevent unrecognized capital waste.

div.class: card p-4 shadow-sm border-0 bg-white mb-3 doc-section-card
div.data-keywords: evidence packs audit preparation certificates affidavits export bundles audit readiness supporting documents
div.p: Evidence packs act as the operational bridge between live compliance activity and audit readiness. Instead of manually scrambling to gather certificates, affidavits, and matching invoices when review season arrives, the module compiles these dependencies into verifiable export bundles that can be used as a structured audit narrative.

Each pack groups verified supplier records, active certification metadata, and underlying spend ledgers. This transparency removes operational guesswork, shortens external review time, and reduces the risk of retroactive point rejection because the underlying evidence trail is already assembled in one place.

div.class: card p-4 shadow-sm border-0 bg-white mb-3 doc-section-card
div.data-keywords: metric interpretation glossary spend at risk verification ready fastest path diagnostic metrics definitions glossary
div.p: Interpreting the interface metrics accurately allows teams to prioritise high-value procurement interventions based on clear financial data rather than intuition. These definitions are intentionally operational so leaders can translate a number into a commercial decision.

ul.li: Spend at Risk The total capital directed toward vendors who currently lack valid documentation or have expired files. This value is vulnerable because an audit performed today would not accept it as verified recognition.
Verification-Ready The safe zone. This is procurement volume backed by current, unexpired, and validated documentation, making it highly likely to count in the scorecard.
Fastest Path The system’s highest-impact improvement route. It surfaces the supplier fixes that unlock the next compliance tier with the least effort and the greatest score movement.

div.class: card p-4 shadow-sm border-0 bg-white mb-3 doc-section-card
div.data-keywords: implementation notes setup dependencies company measurement period rule set import validation data quality support roadmap
div.p: B-good works best when the core reference data is kept clean and current. The module expects a stable company context, an active measurement period, and reliable supplier master data before spend is imported in bulk. If those inputs are weak, the scorecard still calculates, but the output will reflect the underlying data quality rather than a polished operational picture.

The product is designed to sit on top of existing Odoo structures rather than forcing a parallel accounting model. That means implementation is mostly about discipline: consistent supplier naming, current evidence uploads, and a clear ownership chain for who maintains the score inputs.
In a commercial rollout, this section is where admins should look first when a score appears too low, a document upload fails, or a batch does not reconcile into the expected recognition bucket.

div.class: card p-4 shadow-sm border-0 bg-white mb-3 doc-section-card
div.data-keywords: common scenarios examples missing evidence expired certificates disputed supplier low score audit issue
div.p: A typical low-risk scenario is a supplier with a current certificate, a verified recognition percentage, and a clean spend history. In that case, the spend line should flow cleanly into the verification-ready bucket and appear in the scorecard as dependable recognised value.

A more sensitive scenario is when a supplier’s certificate has expired but historic spend remains present in the system. The module should not silently treat that value as safe; instead it should flag the exposure so the business can decide whether to refresh the evidence, move spend, or accept the reduction in recognition.

The most common review problem is not the absence of data but the presence of data that has become stale. That is why the product emphasizes status transitions, expiry visibility, and operational follow-through rather than just list reporting.

div.class: card p-4 shadow-sm border-0 bg-white mb-3 doc-section-card
div.data-keywords: faq edge cases questions troubleshooting why score low how to interpret data support

ul.li: Why can the score move without new spend? Because evidence status changes can alter whether existing spend is recognized, which means a certificate update can improve or reduce the score even when no new invoice is imported.

Why do some suppliers appear risky? A supplier becomes risky when documentation is missing, disputed, or expired. The system surfaces that risk because the related spend cannot be treated as fully defensible.

What happens when data is incomplete? Incomplete data is handled conservatively. The engine prefers to flag exposure rather than overstate compliance, which protects the business from false confidence during verification.
